item.title: Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium — Sun Nov 1, 1:00 PM — Waldron Arts Center
item.description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium ” on stage October 30th- November 15th at the Waldron Auditorium.
Get ready for a frightfully fun adventure with Goosebumps The Musical, based on the wildly popular books by R. L. Stine! When Brooke and Zeke are cast in their school’s spooky new play, The Phantom, they start to wonder if the show is actually cursed. As strange messages appear and rehearsals are disrupted by a mysterious masked figure, they must uncover the truth: is it all an elaborate prank… or is their theater truly haunted? Full of catchy songs, laugh-out-loud moments, and just the right amount of Halloween-season chills, this musical mystery is perfect for kids, tweens, and grown-ups who remember reading by flashlight. Fun for all ages!
See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/goosebumps/ https://seeconstellation.org/k

item.title: Don't Bother to Knock | Matinee Classics — Sun Nov 1, 4:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Hoping to reconcile with his girlfriend Lyn (Anne Bancroft in her screen debut), pilot Jed Towers (Richard Widmark) arrives at the hotel where she works only to be rebuffed. Meanwhile, a fragile young woman named Nell Forbes (Marilyn Monroe) is trying to get a fresh start in life after being in a sanitarium by babysitting for one of the hotel’s families. Striking up a flirtation with Jed, Nell slowly becomes more dangerous as her grasp on reality begins to loosen, revealing a haunting, surprisingly tender portrait of trauma unlike anything else Monroe put on celluloid. [76 min; film noir; English]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Sun PM Worship — Sun Nov 1, 4:00 PM
We the People — Sun Nov 1, 5:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Join the Bloomington Symphony Orchestra https://www.bloomingtonsymphony.com/ as they perform a concert in recognition of our country’s 250th year. From the familiar square dance feel of Copland’s Hoedown, to the soulful, bluesy tonalities of Still’s Afro-American Symphony, this concert explores what it means to be an American.
4:15pm pre-concert talk 5:00pm performance
Program: Aaron Copland – “Hoe-Down” from Rodeo Gary Powell Nash – “In Memoriam Sojourner Truth” Jennifer Higdon – All Things Majestic William Grant Still – Symphony No. 1, “Afro-American”
“I travel the world, and I’m happy to say that America is still the great melting pot – maybe a chunky stew rather than a melting pot at this point, but you know what I mean.” – Philip Glass, 1999 NPR interview
BSO Season Passes can be purchased until October 16th. Passes include discounted tickets to all 4 season concerts, reserved seating, and other benefits. To learn more and purchase your Season Pass CLICK HERE https://www.bloom

item.title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building — Sat Nov 21, 9:15 AM
item.description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar. Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30. Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road parking lot. The gate is open. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd. Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)
